name: Von der Decken's Hornbill (德氏弯嘴犀鸟)
Muscovy Duck (番鸭)
description: The Muscovy Duck (Cairina moschata) is a large waterfowl, with males reaching up to 15 lb, displaying black plumage with iridescent green highlights, red facial caruncles, and color variations such as white or brown. It is a strong perch‑percher, relatively silent, and feeds on plants and small animals, thriving in both tropical and urban habitats.

name: Black-throated Blue Warbler
description: The Black-throated Blue Warbler is a small songbird with a dark blue back, black throat and sides, and a white belly. It has a rounded wing shape, a notched or square-tipped tail, and measures about 6 inches in size.

name: Black-throated Green Warbler
description: The Black-throated Green Warbler is a small songbird with a bright yellow face, black throat, and greenish back. It has a rounded wing shape, a notched or square-tipped tail, and measures about 5 inches in size.

name: Cedar Waxwing (雪松太平鸟)
description: The Cedar Waxwing (Bombycilla cedrorum) is a medium-sized, sleek bird about 8 inches long, with a large head, short neck, and short, wide bill, featuring soft pastel colors, a distinctive flat crest, and a tail that can appear yellow or orange. It is social, nomadic, and often seen in flocks year‑round, feeding primarily on berries.

name: Yellow-breasted Chat
description: The Yellow-breasted Chat is a large songbird with a vibrant yellow chest and throat, olive-green upper body, and white belly. It has a sturdy bill, long rounded tail, and distinct white spectacle marking around its eyes. It is approximately 8 inches in size and is known for its unique vocalizations.

name: Red-tailed Hawk (红尾鵟)
description: The Red‑tailed Hawk is a large North American raptor about 25 inches long with a wingspan up to 56 inches, featuring a distinctive red tail, brown‑red‑white‑yellow plumage, and a broad, rounded wing shape. It soars and flies directly, hunting small mammals, birds, and reptiles, and is known for its keen vision and loud, raspy call.

name: Eastern Wood-Pewee (东绿霸鹟)
description: The Eastern Wood-Pewee (Contopus virens) is a small flycatcher with gray-green upperparts and pale underparts. It has a size of 7 inches and is known for its distinctive song that sounds like "pee-a-wee."

name: Eastern Bluebird (东蓝鸲)
description: The Eastern Bluebird (Sialia sialis) is a small bird with a bright blue back, rust or brick-red throat and breast, and white belly. It is about 8 inches in size and is known for its melodious song.

name: Black-and-White Warbler (黑白森莺)
description: The Black-and-White Warbler is a small, six‑inch bird with striking black and white vertical stripes and a long, thin bill. It inhabits North American forests, forages on tree trunks like nuthatches, and migrates to warmer regions during winter.

name: Blackpoll Warbler
description: The Blackpoll Warbler is a small songbird known for its distinctive appearance, including a black cap, white cheeks, and streaked back during the breeding season. It has a wingspan of approximately 6 inches and undertakes one of the longest overwater migratory journeys of any songbird, flying non-stop over the Atlantic Ocean from its breeding grounds in North America to its wintering grounds in South America.

name: Canada Warbler
description: The Canada Warbler (Setophaga ruticilla) is a small songbird with slate-grey upperparts, yellow underparts, and a distinctive necklace of black streaks. They have relatively long tails that they flick frequently. They are found in dense, wet, and mossy habitats, especially during breeding season, and are known for their distinctive song. They are non-migratory but actually migrate to South America for the winter. They are currently listed as a threatened species due to habitat loss and fragmentation.

name: Flaco (Eurasian eagle owl)
description: Flaco is a Eurasian Eagle Owl, belonging to the species Bubo bubo. They are one of the largest species of owls, with a wingspan that can reach up to 180 cm and a height of up to 75 cm. They have distinctive ear tufts and bright orange eyes. Their plumage varies in color, generally having a mix of mottled brown, black, and tawny.

name: Laughing Gull (笑鸥)
description: The Laughing Gull (Leucophaeus atricilla) is a medium-sized water bird, about 18 inches long, with a sleek gray body, black head, and white eye arcs that turn white in winter. It feeds on fish, insects, and crustaceans, often scavenging near coasts, and is known for its distinctive high‑pitched laughing call.

name: Northern Waterthrust
description: The Northern Waterthrush is a small New World warbler with a size of 6 inches. It is brown on top, white below with streaks on its chest, and has a strong white eyebrow and a large bill.

name: Wilson’s Warbler
description: The Wilson's Warbler is a small songbird with vibrant yellow plumage and a distinctive black cap on males. They have a rounded wing shape, a notched, rounded, or square-tipped tail, and measure about 5 inches in size.

name: Tufted Titmouse (冠山雀）
description: The Tufted Titmouse is a small, energetic perching bird about 6 inches long, with soft gray plumage, a black forehead, and bright rust-colored flanks, plus a distinctive crest. It has rounded wings and a square‑tipped tail, enabling direct flight and frequent flittering among trees.

name: Hooded Warbler
description: The Hooded Warbler is a small songbird with a size of 6 inches. It has a distinct coloration, with males having bright yellow faces, a black hood and bib, and females and juveniles having an olive-green cap extending to the back of their necks.

name: Magnolia Warbler
description: The Magnolia Warbler (Setophaga magnolia) is a small songbird with a size of 5 inches. It has striking yellow and black plumage, with yellow underparts, gray or black back, and a black mask in breeding males.

name: American Coot (美洲白骨顶)
description: The American Coot (Fulica americana) is a medium‑sized water bird about 40 cm (16 inches) long, with a dark gray‑to‑black body, white beak, and distinctive red eye. It inhabits North American wetlands, is omnivorous, and walks on land using broad lobed scales instead of webbed feet.

name: Great Blue Heron (大蓝鹭)
description: The Great Blue Heron is a large wading bird about 24 inches tall with a long, curved neck, pointed yellow‑orange beak, and grey‑blue feathers; its wingspan can reach up to 6 feet. It is a solitary predator that hunts by standing motionless on water’s edge, feeding on fish, amphibians, shrimp, crabs, rodents, small mammals, and occasionally other birds.

name: White-eyed Vireo (白眼莺雀)
description: The White-eyed Vireo is a small perching bird with a bright yellow-green body, distinctive white eyes, and a yellow "spectacles" pattern around its eyes. It has a rounded wing shape, a notched or square-tipped tail shape, and measures about 5 inches in size.

name: Hairy woodpecker (长嘴啄木鸟)
description: The Hairy Woodpecker is a medium-sized woodpecker measuring approximately 7-10 inches in length. It has a predominantly black and white plumage with a bold white stripe down its back and white underparts.

name: Greater Yellowlegs
description: The Greater Yellowlegs is a large shorebird with long, bright yellow legs. It has a slim, straight bill, mottled gray-brown body, and a white belly. It is an active forager often seen running or hopping in shallow water while feeding. It is a long-distance migrant, breeding in the boreal forest and wintering along the coasts of North and South America. It primarily consumes insects but can also eat small fish and crustaceans.

name: Yellow Warbler
description: The Yellow Warbler is a bright yellow bird with a rounded head and thin, pointed bill. It is approximately 5 inches in size and known for its sweet, high-pitched song.

name: Black-crowned Night Heron (夜鹭)
description: The Black‑crowned Night Heron (Nycticorax nycticorax) is a medium‑sized wading bird about 28 inches long, featuring a black crown, dark back, white‑grey body, red eyes, yellow legs, and pale grey wings. It is nocturnal/crepuscular, feeds on small fish, crustaceans, amphibians, insects and small mammals, and nests in colonies on sticks or the ground.

name: Palm Warbler (棕榈莺)
description: The Palm Warbler is a small songbird with a yellow body, olive-brown back, and a rusty-red cap. It is about 6 inches in size and is known for its constant tail wagging behavior and foraging on the ground.

name: Blue Jay (冠蓝鸦)
description: The Blue Jay (Cyanocitta cristata) is a 14‑inch (35 cm) perching bird with bright blue upperparts, white underparts, a blue crest, and distinctive black markings on its neck and throat. It is an intelligent, adaptable omnivore known for direct flight, aggressive nest defense, and loud, jay‑like calls.

name: Great Horned Owl
description: The Great Horned Owl, or Bubo virginianus, is a large bird known for its distinct "ear" tufts and white throat. It has a size of approximately 25 inches and can be identified by its horizontal bars across the belly.

name: Brown Creeper
description: The Brown Creeper (Certhia americana) is a small bird with distinctive brown and white plumage. It has a slender, down-curved bill and a stiff tail. It is about 6 inches in size and is known for its flittering and undulating behavior.

name: Downy woodpecker (绒啄木鸟)
description: The Downy Woodpecker is the smallest North American woodpecker, about 6 inches long, with black, white and red plumage, a white belly, black wings spotted with white, and males have a small red patch on the back of their head. It moves rapidly on tree trunks, feeds mainly on insects (also seeds and berries), and thrives in a variety of habitats from forests to urban backyards.

name: American Redstart (橙尾鸲莺)
description: The American Redstart is a distinctive North American warbler known for its striking coloration, including black bodies and bright patches of orange-red on their wings, flanks, and tail. They are approximately 6 inches in size and are highly territorial and vocal, with a series of high-pitched, rapid notes as their song.

name: Song Sparrow (北美歌雀)
description: The Song Sparrow is a medium-sized bird about 7 inches long, with brown, gray, and white coloration and a long, rounded tail. It inhabits open, shrubby, and wet areas across North America, feeding on insects and seeds while known for its varied, melodious song.

name: Black Skimmer (黑剪嘴鸥)
description: The Black Skimmer (Rynchops niger) is a medium to large water bird about 20 inches (40‑50 cm) long with a distinctive long lower mandible, black back and cap, white underparts, and bright red/orange bill and legs. It skims coastal waters in a direct flight, using its unique beak to catch fish, and is known for its harsh, dog‑like bark.

name: Mourning Dove (哀鸽)
description: The Mourning Dove is a medium-sized North American bird, 9‑13 inches long, with a light grey‑brown body, a slightly pink chest, and a long, pointed tail with white edges. It has a swift, direct flight, a mournful cooing call, and feeds mainly on seeds and grains.

name: Herring Gull (银鸥)
description: The Herring Gull (*Larus argentatus*) is a large gull about 26 inches long, with pale grey wings, white underparts, a yellow bill featuring a red tip, and pinkish legs. It inhabits coasts and inland waters across North America, Europe, and Western Asia, feeding on fish, invertebrates, and urban waste while emitting a loud, laughing call.

name: Chipping Sparrow (棕顶雀鹀)
description: The Chipping Sparrow (Spizella passerina) is a small perching bird about 6 inches long, characterized by a warm rufous cap, black eye line, and gray‑brown streaked upperparts with pale underparts. It inhabits open woodlands and forests, feeds on insects during breeding season and seeds otherwise, and is known for its simple, dry, insect‑like trill.

name: Red-winged Blackbird (红翅黑鹂)
description: The Red-winged Blackbird (Agelaius phoeniceus) is a medium-sized bird with black feathers, distinctive red and yellow shoulder patches, and a loud conk-la-ree! song. It is approximately 9 inches in size and primarily found in wetlands, where it is highly territorial.

name: Spotted Sandpiper (斑腹矶鹬)
description: The Spotted Sandpiper (Actitis macularia) is a small, 8‑inch wading bird with black, brown, orange, and white plumage, known for its rapid wingbeats, direct flight, and distinctive teetering, tail‑bobbing gait. It is migratory, solitary, and wary, inhabiting North American shorelines in summer and wintering across Central and South America.

name: Wood Duck (林鸳鸯)
description: The Wood Duck (Aix sponsa) is a striking waterbird about 20 inches long, with iridescent green, chestnut, blue, brown, orange, red, white, yellow plumage and a distinctive patterned head. It lives in wooded swamps, nests in tree cavities or nest boxes, perches on branches using strong claws, and feeds on fruits, aquatic plants, and invertebrates.

name: Red-eyed Vireo (红眼莺雀)
description: The Red-eyed Vireo is a small, robust bird with olive-green upperparts, white underparts, and a grey crown. It is approximately 13-14 cm long with a wingspan of 24-27 cm.

name: Canada Goose (加拿大鹅)
description: The Canada Goose is a large water bird about 46 inches long, with black, brown, gray, and white plumage, a long black neck, black head, white chinstrap, and a black tail featuring a white U‑shaped band. It shows direct flight, migratory behavior, lives in flocks, and feeds mainly on grass, grains, and berries.

name: House Finch (家朱雀)
description: The House Finch is a small, 6‑inch perching bird with warm red, brown, and streaky plumage, a square‑tipped tail, and a heavy conical bill. It is gregarious, often found in urban and suburban areas, feeding on grains, seeds, and berries, and is known for its joyous warble.

name: Veery
description: The Veery is a bird species with warm cinnamon-brown upperparts, pinkish-buff underparts, and a rounded tail. It has a size of around 8 inches and is known for its ethereal song.

name: Green-winged Teal (美洲绿翅鸭)
description: A small water bird measuring about 15 inches, the Green-winged Teal (Anas crecca) displays vibrant plumage with brown, gray, green, red, white, and yellow colors and a distinctive green speculum. It has a pointed, tapered wing, rounded short wedge‑shaped tail, and exhibits direct, non‑migratory flight.

name: Broad-winged Hawk
description: The Broad-winged Hawk measures about 34–44 cm (13–17 in) in length with a wingspan of 75–100 cm (30–39 in). It has a dark brown upper body, barred underparts, a short wide tail with white bands, and a distinctive dark line from beak to eyes.

name: European Starling (欧洲椋鸟)
description: European Starling is a medium‑sized passerine about 8 inches long, with black plumage showing purple‑green iridescence and winter white speckles. It is noted for direct flight, rapid wingbeats, complex vocal mimicry, and large communal roosts and murmurations.

name: Winter Wren
description: The Winter Wren, also known as the Eurasian Wren, is a small bird with a short and stubby body, rounded wings, and a short tail. It has a uniform dark brown color and is known for its rapid flight and powerful voice.

name: American Crow (美洲鸦)
description: The American Crow (Corvus brachyrhynchos) is a large, predominantly black perching bird about 22 inches long with broad, fingered, rounded wings and a short, square‑tipped tail. It is highly intelligent, social, and adaptable, inhabiting varied North American habitats and feeding on a diverse omnivorous diet.

name: Northern Shoveler (琵嘴鸭)
description: The Northern Shoveler (Anas clypeata) is a 20‑inch water bird with a distinctive large, spoon‑shaped bill and striking coloration—males show a green head, yellow eyes, and chestnut flanks, while females are mottled brown. It feeds by filtering aquatic invertebrates and plants, exhibits direct and erratic flight, and is non‑migratory despite occasional seasonal movements.

name: Ring-necked Duck (环颈潜鸭)
description: The Ring‑necked Duck is a medium‑sized diving duck (~18 inches long) with a glossy black back, slate‑gray body, and a distinctive white ring on the bill plus a chestnut neck ring. It inhabits freshwater ponds and lakes, migrates seasonally between boreal Canada and the southern U.S./Central America, and feeds on aquatic insects, plants, and seeds.

name: Least Flycatcher
description: The Least Flycatcher, scientifically known as Empidonax minimus, is one of the smallest flycatchers found in North America. It has olive green upper parts, bold white eye rings and wing bars, whitish to pale yellow underparts, and a distinctive "che-bek" call.

name: Baltimore Oriole (橙腹拟黄鹂)
description: The Baltimore Oriole (Icterus galbula) is an 8‑inch (20 cm) perching bird with vibrant black, green, orange, white, and yellow plumage; males display a bright orange‑golden chest and belly, while females are more muted. It has rounded wings, a square‑tipped rounded tail, and exhibits direct flight behavior.

name: House Sparrow (家麻雀)
description: The House Sparrow measures about 16 cm (6.3 in) in length and weighs 24–39.5 g, featuring brown‑grey plumage, a short tail, and a stout bill. It is a highly social, urban‑adapted bird commonly found in human‑made environments.

name: Bay-breasted Warbler
description: The Bay-breasted Warbler is a small songbird with a chestnut-brown head and neck, black face, and grey back. It has a size of 5.5 inches and is known for its distinctive song and migration to Central and South America during winter.

name: Osprey (鱼鹰)
description: The Osprey (Pandion haliaetus) is a large raptor about 24 in (60 cm) long with a wingspan up to 71 in (180 cm), featuring brown upperparts, greyish head and underparts, a black eye patch, and long, fingered wings. It is a diurnal, fish‑eating bird found near water, known for direct flight, soaring, and excellent fishing abilities.

name: Northern Cardinal (北美红雀)
description: The Northern Cardinal (Cardinalis cardinalis) is a mid-sized songbird about 9 inches (23 cm) long, featuring a distinctive crest, a black facial mask in females and a bright red plumage in males. It inhabits southern Canada, the eastern United States, and parts of Central America, commonly found in backyards, parks, and shrubs.

name: Rose-breasted Grosbeak
description: The Rose-breasted Grosbeak is a large seed-eating bird with a robust beak. The males have black and white coloration with a rose-red patch on their chest, while the females are brown and heavily striped.

name: Snowy Egret (雪鹭)
description: The Snowy Egret is a small to medium-sized heron about 26 inches long, with distinctive white plumage, black legs, and bright yellow feet. It inhabits shallow waters, feeds mainly on fish, and flies swiftly with direct, steady wing beats.

name: Northern Rough-winged Swallow (中北美毛翅燕)
description: The Northern Rough-winged Swallow is a small bird with rugged, brownish-gray plumage and a white underbody. It has broad, long, pointed, and tapered wings and a notched, square-tipped tail. It is approximately 6 inches in size.

name: Barn Swallow (家燕)
description: The Barn Swallow is a sleek, agile bird with a distinct long, forked tail. It has a glossy steel blue upper body, a pale buffy or cinnamon wash on its underparts, and a dark chestnut forehead and throat with a broad dark blue band across the chest. It is approximately 7 inches in size.

name: Chestnut-sided Warbler
description: The Chestnut-sided Warbler is a small bird, measuring about 6 inches in size. It has a distinctive color pattern with chestnut-colored streaks on its white underparts, a yellow crown, and a black eye line. Its upper parts are predominantly gray-green, and it has a pointed beak suited for its insectivorous diet. This energetic bird is known for its flitting behavior and the males have a distinct song during the breeding season. It is non-migratory but breeds in North America and winters in Central and South America.

name: Evening Grosbeak
description: The Evening Grosbeak is a large finch with a heavy, thick bill. Males have a vibrant yellow coloration with a black tail and wings marked by a large white patch, while females have grayish hues with a yellow tinge on the neck and head. They are approximately 8 inches in size.

name: Great Black-backed Gull (大黑背鸥)
description: The Great Black-backed Gull (Larus marinus) is the world’s largest gull, measuring about 32 inches (64–79 cm) in length with a wingspan of 1.5–1.7 m. It has a powerful build, black back and wings, white underparts, pink legs, a heavy yellow bill with a red spot, and a pale yellow eye.

name: Blackburnian Warbler
description: The Blackburnian Warbler is a small bird, measuring about 5 inches in size. It has a black and white body with a fiery orange throat, orange-red face, and two white wing bars.

name: American Kestrel (美洲隼)
description: The American Kestrel, also known as the "Sparrow Hawk," is the smallest and most common falcon in North America. It has a reddish back and tail, contrasting with a white belly, and both sexes have black vertical "sideburns" on the sides of their heads. The bird is approximately 12 inches in size.

name: Nashville Warbler (黄喉虫森莺)
description: The Nashville Warbler is a small songbird with a bright yellow belly, olive-green back, gray head with a white eye-ring, and a chestnut cap on males. It is about 5 inches in size and known for its energetic behavior and beautiful song.

name: Blue-headed Vireo (蓝头莺雀)
description: The Blue-headed Vireo is a small songbird with a blue-grey head, white eye spectacles, olive green back, and white underparts with green streaks. It has a size of 5 inches.

name: Ruby-throated Hummingbird (红喉北蜂鸟)
description: The Ruby‑throated Hummingbird is a tiny bird about 3.5 in (7‑9 cm) long, weighing roughly 3 g, with a bright red male throat, green upperparts, and grey‑white underparts. It feeds on nectar with a slender bill, is aggressive at feeders, and migrates between Eastern North America and Central America.

name: Gray Catbird (灰嘲鸫)
description: The Gray Catbird is a 9‑inch perching bird with slate‑gray plumage, a black cap, chestnut under‑tail coverts, and occasional orange or red highlights. It exhibits direct flight, flittering behavior, and a distinctive cat‑like mewling call.

name: Tree Swallow (双色树燕)
description: The Tree Swallow is a sleek, fast-flying bird with iridescent blue-green upperparts and clean white underparts. It has long, pointed wings and a size of approximately 6 inches.

name: Monk Parakeet (和尚鹦鹉)
description: The Monk Parakeet measures about 11‑12 inches (28‑30 cm) in length and has a bright green body with grey‑blue on the forehead and chest. It is a social, tree‑climbing bird known for building large communal twig nests.

name: Swainson’s Thrush
description: The Swainson's Thrush, scientifically known as Catharus ustulatus, is a medium-sized thrush with warm, buffy-brown upperparts and distinctly spotted underparts. It has a round shape, long wings, and a slender bill. The bird is approximately 8 inches in size and is known for its ethereal, fluting song heard in twilight forests and northern woods.

name: House Wren
description: The House Wren (Troglodytes aedon) is a small bird measuring about 5 inches in size. It has brown, gray, and tan plumage, rounded wings, and a round and short tail.

name: Eastern Towhee (棕肋唧鹀)
description: The Eastern Towhee is a 9‑inch perching bird with striking black, brown, orange, red, tan, and white plumage; males have a black hood and back with rufous sides, while females are brown where males are black. It lives in brushy woodlands, feeds on ground insects and seeds using a unique two‑footed backward hop, and is non‑migratory.

name: Mallard (绿头鸭)
description: The Mallard (Anas platyrhynchos) is a medium‑sized waterbird about 20–26 inches (50–65 cm) long, with males having a bright green head and both sexes displaying a blue‑purple speculum on the wings. It is an omnivorous, migratory duck known for dabbling feeding behavior and a distinctive loud quack, especially in females.

name: Cape May Warbler
description: The Cape May Warbler is a small bird measuring about 5 inches in size. It has a yellowish-brown body with bold streaks of black, a distinctive chestnut-colored cheek patch, and a unique semi-tubular tongue for sipping nectar efficiently.

name: Yellow-rumped Warbler (黄腰莺)
description: The Yellow-rumped Warbler is a medium-sized (≈6 inches) perching bird with a distinctive yellow rump, black, blue, brown, gray, white, and yellow plumage, a streaked grey‑brown back, brown wings with two white wing bars, and white underparts marked by black side streaks. It forages by flipping leaves and can digest waxes from bayberries, allowing it to winter far north, and its song is a loose, variable trill with a sharp check call.

name: Little Blue Heron (小蓝鹭)
description: The Little Blue Heron is a medium‑sized, slate‑blue heron with a purple‑tinged neck, black and blue bill, and dark wings, measuring about 24 inches in length. It inhabits shallow marshes and lagoons across the Americas, feeding on small fish, crustaceans, and insects.

name: Yellow-bellied Sapsucker
description: The Yellow-bellied Sapsucker is a medium-sized woodpecker (8 inches) with black and white plumage, bold white wing stripes, a red forehead and throat, and a pale yellow wash on the belly. It is known for its unique feeding habits of drilling holes in tree bark to feed on sap and insects.

name: Fox Sparrow
description: The Fox Sparrow is a large, stocky sparrow about 7 inches long, with gray‑brown upperparts, reddish streaks, and heavily spotted underparts giving it a fox‑like appearance. It inhabits dense woodland thickets, feeds on seeds, berries, and insects, and is known for its melodious, whistling song.

name: Field Sparrow (田雀鹀)
description: The Field Sparrow is a small 6‑inch perching bird with reddish‑brown upperparts, plain pinkish‑gray underparts, a distinctive eye‑ring, and a pinkish bill. It inhabits open fields and grasslands, feeding on seeds, fruits, and insects while remaining shy and close to cover.

name: Red-bellied Woodpecker (红腹啄木鸟)
description: The Red‑bellied Woodpecker is a medium‑sized bird about 9 inches long, featuring black, white, red, and tan plumage with a distinctive red belly, cap, and nape, and a sharp chisel‑like bill. It inhabits Eastern woodlands, forages on trees and the ground, and is known for its loud rolling churr call and rapid drumming.

name: American Goldfinch (美洲金翅雀)
description: The American Goldfinch, also known as the Eastern Goldfinch, is a small bird with vibrant yellow plumage in the summer and a drab, olive-brown coloration in the winter. It has a rounded wing shape, a notched tail shape, and measures about 5 inches in size.

name: Common Nighthawk
description: The Common Nighthawk (Chordeiles minor) is a unique bird primarily found in North and Central America. It has a mottled pattern of black, white, buff, and gray, and measures approximately 10 inches in size.

name: Fish Crow (鱼鸦)
description: The Fish Crow is an 18‑inch perching bird with a glossy black plumage that can appear slightly purple or blue in light. It inhabits wetland areas of the eastern and southeastern United States, exhibiting direct flight and soaring behavior.

name: American Black Duck (北美黑鸭)
description: The American Black Duck is a large dabbling water bird about 20 inches long, with dark brown to black plumage, a lighter chest, yellow‑green bill, and a purple speculum on the wings during breeding. It inhabits wooded swamps and coastal marshes in eastern North America and is largely non‑migratory.

name: American Robin (美洲知更鸟)
description: The American Robin, scientifically known as Turdus migratorius, is a migratory songbird measuring about 11 inches in size. It has a warm orange belly, dark gray-brown upper body, and is known for its beautiful caroling song.

name: Eastern Phoebe (东菲比霸鹟)
description: The Eastern Phoebe is a small bird with dusky gray-brown plumage, a slightly darker head, and no eye-ring. It has a distinctive "phoebe" call and a habit of wagging its tail when perched. It measures about 7 inches in size.

name: Common Yellowthroat (黄喉地莺)
description: The Common Yellowthroat is a small bird with a size of 5 inches. It is known for its bright yellow throat and chest, black "bandit's mask" across the eyes of males, and olive-green back.

name: Indigo Bunting (靛蓝彩鹀)
description: The Indigo Bunting is a small North American bird, about 6 inches long, with vibrant electric‑blue plumage in breeding males and more subdued brown in females and non‑breeding individuals. It feeds mainly on seeds and insects, prefers open habitats with shrubs, and migrates long distances between North America and Central America.

name: Rock Pigeon (原鸽)
description: The Rock Pigeon is a robust, short‑necked bird with a slender bill, typically gray with a glossy neck, orange or red eyes ringed in white, and purplish‑red feet. It measures about 13 inches (34‑37 cm) in length and weighs 238‑380 g.

name: Bald Eagle (白头海雕)
description: The Bald Eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a large raptor about 40 inches (100 cm) long with a broad, fingered wingspan over 2 m, featuring a distinctive white head, dark brown body, and yellow beak. It lives near water, feeds mainly on fish, has keen vision, is non‑migratory, and is a symbol of the United States.

name: Caspian Tern (里海海鸥)
description: The Caspian Tern is the world’s largest tern, measuring about 24 inches in length with a thick red bill tipped dark, a white body, pale‑grey upper wings, and a black cap in breeding season. It flies gracefully, soaring and direct, and is known for its harsh, crow‑like “kraaak” call.

name: Northern Flicker (北扑翅䴕)
description: The Northern Flicker is a medium-sized woodpecker about 13 inches long, with brown plumage, a spotted underbelly, black‑scalloped back, and a distinctive white rump patch visible in flight. It feeds mainly on ants and beetles on the ground and inhabits woodlands, suburbs, and parks across North America.

name: Golden-crowned Kinglet (金冠戴菊)
description: The Golden-crowned Kinglet is a very small (4 in) perching bird with an olive‑green body, a yellow‑orange crown patch, and two white wing bars. It inhabits coniferous forests, feeds on insects, spiders, seeds and berries, and is known for rapid wingbeats, flittering flight, and a high‑pitched song.

name: American Woodcock
description: The American Woodcock, also known as the 'timberdoodle,' is a small, chunky bird with mottled gray/brown plumage. It has a long, straight bill and large, black eyes. It is about 12 inches in size and known for its unique courtship ritual called the 'sky dance.'

name: Northern Parula (北美森莺)
description: The Northern Parula is a small warbler with a blue-gray upper body, greenish back patch, and two white wing bars. It is around 5 inches in size and is known for its strikingly colorful appearance.

name: Common Grackle (普通擬八哥)
description: The Common Grackle is a large, 12‑inch perching bird with a glossy black body that can show blue, purple, or bronze iridescence and bright yellow eyes. It is omnivorous, non‑migratory, and often found in flocks across diverse habitats such as forests, farmlands, and urban areas.

name: Prairie Warbler
description: The Prairie Warbler is a small songbird with a size of 5 inches. It has yellow underparts, streaks of black on its sides, olive green back with faint black streaks, and a distinctive pattern on its face with black lines running through the eyes and along the sides of the throat.

name: Ruddy Duck
description: A small, stout freshwater duck about 16 inches long, with a bright blue bill, chestnut body in breeding plumage and gray‑brown winter feathers, plus a black cap, white cheek patches, and a long spiky tail. It is migratory, found in North American marshes, ponds, and lakes, and is known for its distinctive courtship behavior.

name: Brant (黑雁)
description: The Brant (Branta bernica) is a medium‑sized water bird about 26 inches long, featuring a black‑brown body, black head, neck, and upper breast with a distinctive white “necklace.” It flies in direct, formation patterns, has pointed tapered wings, a short rounded square‑tipped tail, and is migratory.

name: Ruby-crowned Kinglet (红冠戴菊)
description: The Ruby‑crowned Kinglet is a tiny 4‑inch bird with olive‑green plumage, white wing bars, a white eye‑ring, and a hidden ruby‑red crown that appears when excited. It constantly flutters between branches, often hanging upside‑down to feed on insects, and is known for its loud, complex song.

name: White-throated Sparrow (白喉带鹀)
description: The White‑throated Sparrow is a 6‑inch perching bird with bold white throat and head stripes, a dark gray‑brown body, black and brown streaked back, and a yellow lores spot. It displays flittering, rapid wingbeats, a broad wing, and a notched‑rounded‑square‑tipped tail.

name: Black-capped Chickadee (黑顶山雀)
description: The Black‑capped Chickadee is a small North American songbird about 5 inches long, with black, gray, tan, and white plumage, a rounded wing shape and a notched, rounded, square‑tipped tail. It exhibits flittering, rapid wingbeats, undulating flight, and can lower its body temperature in cold winters while showing strong spatial memory for food caches.

name: Eastern Kingbird (东方王霸鹟)
description: The Eastern Kingbird is a large flycatcher with a steel gray upper body, white underparts, and a black tail with a white tip. It has a stout bill and is known for its aggressive behavior towards larger birds. It is approximately 8 inches in size.

name: Mute Swan (疣鼻天鹅)
description: The Mute Swan (Cygnus olor) is a large, primarily white water bird with a distinctive orange beak, measuring about 150 cm (60 inches) in length. It is non‑migratory, often seen in lakes and ponds, and displays direct flight in formation while being of low conservation concern.

name: Double-crested Cormorant (双冠鸬鹚)
description: The Double‑crested Cormorant (Phalacrocorax auritus) is a large waterbird about 36 inches long, with a stocky body, long neck, broad rounded wings, and a long wedge‑shaped tail. It is black or dark brown, develops a distinctive double crest of white or black feathers during breeding, and has bright blue eyes with orange‑yellow facial skin.

name: American Wigeon
description: The American Wigeon is a medium‑sized dabbling duck about 23 inches long, featuring a white forehead, green crown band, brown body and a pale‑blue bill tipped in black. It feeds on water and land, grazing on aquatic plants and insects, and breeds in northern grasslands and wetlands.

name: Red-headed Woodpecker (红头啄木鸟)
description: The Red‑headed Woodpecker is a medium‑sized bird about 10 inches long, with a striking red head and neck, white underparts, and black back and wings. It inhabits eastern U.S. woodlands and farmlands, displays direct flight, and uniquely catches insects in flight while storing food in crevices.

name: Pine Warbler (松莺)
description: The Pine Warbler is a small bird with yellow plumage, dark stripes, and a size of 6 inches. It is known for its preference for pine forests and its powerful trill song.

name: White-breasted Nuthatch (白胸䴓)
description: The white‑breasted nuthatch is a small, stocky songbird about 6 inches long, with a black cap, white face, chest and belly, slate‑gray back, and black wings marked by white patches. It moves by “walking” down tree trunks, feeds mainly on insects (also seeds and nuts), and emits a loud, nasal yank‑yank call.

name: Hermit Thrush
description: The Hermit Thrush is a medium-sized bird with rich brown upper parts, smudged spots on the breast, and a reddish tail. It is known for its beautiful, ethereal song and prefers to live in dense forests, feeding on insects and berries.

name: Carolina Wren (卡罗苇鹪鹩)
description: The Carolina Wren is a small, chunky bird about 6 inches long with a round body, long tail, and bright reddish‑brown upperparts, warm buffy‑orange underparts, a white eyebrow stripe, and white chin and throat. It is industrious, bold, and vocal, frequently foraging on the ground, climbing trunks, and exploring cavities within its territory.

name: Warbling Vireo
description: The Warbling Vireo is a small songbird with a light gray head and neck, olive-green upper parts, and white underparts with a hint of yellow. It has a rounded wing shape, a notched and square-tipped tail, and measures about 5 inches in size.

name: Belted Kingfisher (白腹鱼狗)
description: The Belted Kingfisher is a large, striking waterbird with a blue‑gray upper body, broad white collar, and a rusty belly band in females, known for its distinct rattling call and skilled hunting of small fish. It measures about 14 inches in length and exhibits direct flight, hovering, and flap/glide flight patterns.

name: Pied-billed Grebe
description: A small, stocky waterbird about 15 inches long with a chicken‑like bill, dark brown upperparts, paler underparts, a thick neck and a hunched appearance. It has large, rear‑placed feet for excellent swimming and diving, rarely flies, and prefers to escape predators by submerging.

name: Cooper’s Hawk (库氏鹰)
description: The Cooper’s Hawk (Accipiter cooperii) is a medium‑sized raptor about 12 inches (30 cm) long, with slate‑gray back, dark cap, red eyes, and short, rounded wings plus a long, rounded tail. It hunts birds and small mammals in forested habitats, is non‑migratory, and displays both flap/glide and soaring flight.

name: Sharp-shinned Hawk
description: The Sharp‑shinned Hawk is the smallest North American hawk, measuring about 12 inches with short, rounded wings, a long notched tail, and a dark bluish‑gray back with a rusty, barred underside. It is highly agile, inhabits forested areas, and preys on birds and small mammals.

name: Hooded Merganser (棕胁秋沙鸭)
description: The Hooded Merganser is a small, striking duck about 20 inches long, with a black, brown, and white body and a distinctive white, fan‑shaped crest that can be expanded to show bold black‑white patterning. It is a diving water bird that feeds on fish, has a third eyelid for underwater vision, and nests in tree cavities, with chicks becoming independent within 24 hours.

name: Great Egret (大白鹭)
description: The Great Egret (Ardea alba) is a large wading bird about 104 cm (41 in) tall, with pure white plumage, black legs, and a beak featuring a bright yellow base. It has long, fingered wings, a short tail, and lives in coasts, lakes, rivers, and wetlands where it hunts fish and small aquatic animals.

name: Scarlet Tanager
description: The Scarlet Tanager is a medium-sized American songbird with a brilliant scarlet red plumage (male) and yellowish underparts (female). It has black wings and tail, and is known for its direct flight and distinctive song. The bird is approximately 8 inches in size.

name: Green Heron (美洲绿鹭)
description: The Green Heron (Butorides virescens) is a small wading bird about 22 inches long, featuring dark green, blue‑tinged back feathers, a warm chestnut chest and neck, and a striking deep red eye. It is known for its tool‑using behavior, dropping lures to attract fish, and its loud “skeow” call when disturbed.

name: Blue-winged Warbler
description: The Blue-winged Warbler is a small bird with vibrant blue wings and tail, a sunny yellow body, and a sharp black eye line. It is about 5 inches in size and known for its distinctive 'bee-buzz' song. It migrates to Central America and the Caribbean for the winter months and faces the threat of habitat loss.

name: Brown-headed Cowbird (褐头牛鹂)
description: The Brown-headed Cowbird is an 8‑inch perching bird with a glossy black body, brown head in males, and gray‑brown coloration in females, featuring a short pointed beak. It is known for its gregarious flocks and brood‑parasitism behavior, laying eggs in other birds’ nests.

name: Red-breasted Nuthatch
description: The Red-breasted Nuthatch is a small songbird with a slate-blue back, red underparts, and a black cap. It is about 6 inches in size and known for its agility and acrobatics in tree-clinging behavior.

name: Great Crested Flycatcher (大冠蝇霸鹟)
description: The Great Crested Flycatcher is a large bird with a heavy bill. It has a yellow underbelly, grey throat and upper breast, and a brownish upper body. It is about 8 inches in size and is known for its boisterous calls.

name: Ovenbird
description: The Ovenbird (Seiurus aurocapilla) is a small songbird with an olive-brown upper body and a streaked breast. It has a size of 6 inches and is known for its loud teacher-teacher-teacher song.

name: Wood Thrush
description: The Wood Thrush is a medium-sized bird with a rich brown upper body, white underparts heavily spotted with large, dark spots, and a round head. It is approximately 8 inches in size and known for its flute-like song.

name: Ring-billed Gull (环嘴鸥)
description: The Ring-billed Gull (Larus delawarensis) is a medium-sized gull measuring about 20 inches (49–64 cm) in length, with a white body, grey wings and back, and a distinctive yellow bill marked by a black ring near the tip. It is adaptable, often found near water or urban areas, and exhibits behaviors such as direct flight, hovering, and soaring.

name: Brown Thrasher (褐矢嘲鸫)
description: The Brown Thrasher is a medium-sized bird with distinctive brown and slightly reddish feathers, a long curved beak, and bright yellow eyes. It has a long rufous tail with dark bands and is known for its impressive repertoire of over a thousand song types.
